text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sherlock-v2 canary in us-west-2 experiencing increased 5xx rate (rolling 5m error rate 12% > 5% threshold). Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/sherlock

maria: I'm on it, paging @aj for backup. Taking page.

aj: On call, pulling logs + replaying failing requests.

leo: Quick Q — do we want feature-flag kill or revert? Kill is fastest.

maria: Kill first. Flag: sherlock.v2_enabled. Toggle it? Use:

curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $FF_TOKEN' \
  https://flags.internal/api/flags/sherlock.v2_enabled/disable

maria: running the toggle now.

deploy-bot: Executing flag toggle: sherlock.v2_enabled -> DISABLED (req id: rb-72b)

maria: 200 OK, flag disabled :white_check_mark:

maria: error rate dropping, canary 5m -> 1.2% now.

sachin: great, prepare revert PR for commit abc123 (regression introduced in #4456). I'll cut the revert and push patch to canary for verification.

sachin: PR created: https://git.internal/r/redwood/sherlock/pulls/5678 "revert: abc123 - patch fix"

sachin: deploying revert to canary (small single-commit revert)

deploy-bot: Deploy started: sherlock canary -> commit def456 (revert). CI: passed.

deploy-bot: Deploy complete: canary updated. Health checks: ok.

maria: monitoring — 5xxs back to baseline, 0.8% 5m. Rollout plan: keep flag off, promote revert to prod after 30m of stability.

emma-cs: CS loop — any customer impact? We saw spikes on some orgs.

maria: impact: ~3% of requests for affected customers between 14:12-14:24 UTC, no PII exposure, no data loss. Asking CS to notify top 5 affected customers with status update.

aj: I'll add incident note + timeline to #postmortems, owner @maria. Action items: add guardrail to deploy pipeline to auto-disable canary if 5xx > 5% for 5m and alert on flag change.

maria: assigning follow-ups: create CI guard, add test for header case causing reg. Retrospective scheduled tomorrow 10:00 UTC.

leo: thanks team. passing back to normal ops. :handshake:

incidents-bot: Incident closed (mitigated). Duration: 12m. Reference: INC-2026-0417-01.
